Abolir ; annuler.

examples.text: Le voleur ne met pas en question dans les livres sophistiques la propriété, l’hérédité, les garanties sociales ; il les supprime net.
Le 31 octobre 1887, on avait parlé dans cette assemblée, non de supprimer les fêtes foraines, mais de les rendre impossibles en y interdisant la musique.
Les anciens impôts basés sur le Koran sont supprimés et remplacés par des contributions nouvelles qui seront recueillies par des fonctionnaires spéciaux, au lieu de l'être par les caïds.

Le départ des juifs n’avait pas supprimé les embarras financiers de leurs clients et ceux qui avaient besoin de capitaux n'eurent d'autre ressource que de s'adresser aux prêteurs chrétiens (lombards ou cahorsins).

glosses: Retrancher ; enlever ; ôter.

examples.text: Ainsi, seules les manifestations perméabilisantes objectivées par le Bleu sont supprimées par l’action immédiate des rutosides.
Après avoir totalement désossé l'engin, j'avais savamment vidé le pot d'échappement en supprimant les chicanes et adapté un carburateur récupéré sur la vieille mobylette d'un copain.
Le pot d’échappement a été supprimé sur le tracteur électrique, ce qui offre plus de visibilité à l’opérateur.

glosses: Tuer.

examples.text: On pense naturellement à supprimer l'homme qui gêne comme on pense à écarter une mouche ; à se gratter immédiatement au point cuisant. C'est un réflexe de l'imagination, laquelle est faite pour ces solutions.
Les Martiens, au moyen d’une drogue procurant des rêves magnifiques, supprimaient les malades, les infirmes et les mal nés, de sorte que, chez eux, la pitié était des plus rudimentaires.

glosses: Censurer.

examples.text: Les articles de journaux trop controversés furent supprimés.

glosses: Détruire ; démolir.

examples.text: Le moulin de Montgon ayant été supprimé par suite de la création du canal des Ardennes , outre l'indemnité d’expropriation due au propriétaire , il en était dû une au fermier.

glosses: Effacer, retirer (des données de la mémoire).

examples.text: Supprimer des données d’un disque dur ne signifie pas les faire disparaître ; elles peuvent être récupérer par divers moyens.

glosses: bauliche und andere (auch zeitweilig errichteten) technische oder künstliche Anlagen, Einrichtungen, Aufbauten und Ähnliches beseitigen, zurückbauen

examples.text: Im Mittelalter wurde hier Silber abgebaut.

glosses: (vor allem auch übertragen) verringern, beseitigen; mindern von Hindernissen, die Prozesse behindern

examples.text: Wegen der verschärften Konkurrenzsituation wurden 234 Arbeitsplätze abgebaut.

examples.text: Die Mikroorganismen bauen das Laub zu Humus und Mineralstoffen ab.

glosses: sich körperlich oder geistig zurückentwickeln

examples.text: Oliver hat in letzter Zeit ganz schön abgebaut!

translations.source_sense_description: Abolir, annuler, annihiler.

glosses: To put an end to, especially with force, to crush, do away with; to prohibit, subdue.

examples.text: Political dissent was brutally suppressed.

glosses: To restrain or repress, such as laughter or an expression.

examples.text: I struggled to suppress my smile.

glosses: To exclude undesirable thoughts from one's mind.

examples.text: He unconsciously suppressed his memories of abuse.

glosses: To prevent publication.

examples.text: The government suppressed the findings of their research about the true state of the economy.

glosses: To stop a flow or stream.

examples.text: The rescue team managed to suppress the flow of oil by blasting the drilling hole.
Hot blackcurrant juice mixed with honey may suppress cough.

glosses: To forbid the use of evidence at trial because it is improper or was improperly obtained.
To reduce unwanted frequencies in a signal.
To stop or prevent the enemy from executing unwanted activities like firing, regrouping, observation or others.
To hold in place, to keep low.

translations.source_sense_description: Abolir, annuler, annihiler.

glosses: To end a law, system, institution, custom or practice.

examples.text: Slavery was abolished in the nineteenth century.
The abolition of the death penalty in international law

glosses: To put an end to or destroy, as a physical object; to wipe out.

examples.text: And with thy blood abolish so reproachful blot.
His quick instinctive hand Caught at the hilt, as to abolish him.

glosses: To delete.
To move from one place to another, especially to take away.

examples.text: He removed the marbles from the bag.
Thou ſhalt not remoue thy neghbours marke which they of olde tyme haue ſett in thyne enheritaunce that thou enheretteſt in the londe which the Lorde thy God geueth the to enioye it.
Now that she was rested and had fed from the luncheon tray Mrs. Broome had just removed, she had reverted to her normal gaiety.

glosses: To move from one place to another, especially to take away.
To replace a dish within a course.

examples.text: But Richmond[…]appeared to lose himself in his own reflections. Some pickled crab, which he had not touched, had been removed with a damson pie; and his sister saw[…]that he had eaten no more than a spoonful of that either.

glosses: To murder.
To dismiss a batsman.
To discard, set aside, especially something abstract (a thought, feeling, etc.).

examples.text: Eternall thraldom was to her more liefe, / Then loſſe of chaſtitie, or chaunge of loue : / Dye had ſhe rather in tormenting griefe, / Then any ſhould of falſeneſſe her reproue, / Or looſeneſſe, that ſhe lightly did remoue.

glosses: To depart, to leave; to move oneself or be moved.

examples.text: THenne the kynge dyd doo calle syre Gawayne / syre Borce / syr Lyonel and syre Bedewere / and commaunded them to goo strayte to syre Lucius / and saye ye to hym that hastely he remeue oute of my land / And yf he wil not / bydde hym make hym redy to bataylle and not distresse the poure peple

glosses: To change one's residence or place of business; to move.

examples.text: Till Birnam wood remove to Dunsinane.
Now my life began to be so easy that I began to say to myself that could I but have been safe from more savages, I cared not if I was never to remove from the place where I lived.
Shortly after this, my father removed, and settled in the same county, about ten miles above Greenville.
I am going to remove. / Where are you going to remove to? / I don't know yet. / When will you know?

glosses: To dismiss or discharge from office.

examples.text: The President removed many postmasters.

glosses: The act of removing something.

examples.text: This place should be at once both school and university, not needing a remove to any other house of scholarship.

There is no tree admits of transplantation so well as the Elm, for a tree of twenty years growth will admit of a remove.

glosses: A dish served to replace an earlier one during a meal; a part of a new course.

examples.text: A supper brings up the rear, not forgetting the introductory luncheon, almost equalling in removes the dinner.
An attempt at entrées and removes failed at the first dinner-party.

examples.text: A freeholder is but one remove from a legislator.

This may be carried on to a great length; tho' at the ſame time vve may obſerve, that each remove conſiderably vveakens the relation.

glosses: Emotional distance or indifference.
